text:
$250\mathrm{g}$ solution of $\mathrm{D}$-glucose in water contains $10.8%$ of carbon by weight. The molality of the solution is nearest to

(Given: Atomic Weights are, $\mathrm{H},1\mathrm{u};\mathrm{C},12\mathrm{u};\mathrm{O},16\mathrm{u}$)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Mass of carbon in the solution $=0.108\times 250=27\text{g}$, all of it from glucose.

One mole of $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{12}\mathrm{O}{}_{6}$ ($180\text{g mol}^{-1}$) contains $72\text{g}$ of carbon, so moles of glucose $=\dfrac{27}{72}=0.375\text{mol}$ and mass of glucose $=0.375\times 180=67.5\text{g}$.

Mass of water (solvent) $=250-67.5=182.5\text{g}=0.1825\text{kg}$.

$m=\dfrac{0.375}{0.1825}=2.05\text{mol kg}^{-1}$

This is nearest to 2.06.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift

text:
Given below are two statements.

Statement I: $\mathrm{O}_{2},\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}$, and $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$ are weakly attracted by magnetic field and are magnetized in the same direction as magnetic field.

Statement II: $\mathrm{NaCl}$ and $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ are weakly magnetized in opposite direction to magnetic field.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{O}_{2},\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$ have 2,1 and 5 unpaired electrons respectively, so these are the paramagnetic species. Hence, they are attracted by magnetic field.

$\mathrm{NaCl}$ and $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ are the diamagnetic species so they are repelled by the magnetic field.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift

text:
Given below are two statements. One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.

Assertion A: Energy of $2\mathrm{s}$ orbital of hydrogen atom is greater than that of $2\mathrm{s}$ orbital of lithium.

Reason R: Energies of the orbitals in the same subshell decrease with increase in the atomic number.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
As the atomic number increases then the potential energy of electrons present in same shell becomes more and more negative. And therefore total energy also becomes more negative.

$\mathrm{E}_{\text{total}}=-13.6\frac{\mathrm{z}^{2}}{\mathrm{n}^{2}}\mathrm{eV}$

$\therefore$ Energies of the orbitals in the same subshell decreases with increase in atomic number.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift

text: Boiling point of a $2%$ aqueous solution of a non-volatile solute A is equal to the boiling point of $8%$ aqueous solution of a non-volatile solute B. The relation between molecular weights of A and B is
options: $\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{A}}=4\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{B}}$
$\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{B}}=4\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{A}}$
$\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{A}}=8\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{B}}$
$\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{B}}=8\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{A}}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For $𝐀:100\mathrm{gm}$ solution $\to 2\mathrm{gm}$ solute $\mathrm{A}$

 $\therefore$ Molality $=\frac{2/\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{A}}}{0.098}$

For B : $100\mathrm{gm}$ solution $\to 8\mathrm{gm}$ solute $\mathrm{B}$

$\begin{array}{l} \therefore \text{Molality}=\dfrac{8/\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{B}}}{0.092} \\  \\ \because (\Delta \mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{B}})_{\mathrm{A}}=(\Delta \mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{B}})_{\mathrm{B}} \end{array}$

$\therefore$ Molality of $\mathrm{A}=$ Molality of $\mathrm{B}$

$\therefore \frac{2}{0.098\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{A}}}=\frac{8}{0.092\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{B}}}$

$\frac{2}{98}\times \frac{92}{8}=\frac{M_{A}}{M_{B}}$

$\frac{1}{4.261}=\frac{\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{B}}}$

$\therefore \mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{B}}=4.261\times \mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{A}}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift

text: The incorrect statement is
options: The first ionization enthalpy of K is less than that of Na and Li.
Xe does not have the lowest first ionization enthalpy in its group.
The first ionization enthalpy of element with atomic number 37 is lower than that of the element with atomic number 38.
The first ionization enthalpy of Ga is higher than that of the d-block element with atomic number 30.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
First ionisation enthalpies (in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$) decide each statement.

(A) Down group 1 the atomic size increases: Li (520) > Na (496) > K (419). The statement is correct.

(B) In group 18, radon (1037) has a lower first ionisation enthalpy than xenon (1170), so Xe is not the lowest in its group. The statement is correct.

(C) $Z=37$ is Rb (403) and $Z=38$ is Sr (549); the single $5s$ electron of Rb is removed more easily than an electron from the filled $5s^{2}$ of Sr. The statement is correct.

(D) $Z=30$ is Zn, whose fully filled $3d^{10}4s^{2}$ configuration is stable (906), while Ga (579) loses a single $4p$ electron that is well shielded by the inner electrons. The first ionisation enthalpy of Ga is therefore lower than that of Zn, and the statement is incorrect.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift

text:
Given below are two statements.

Statement I : Iron (III) catalyst, acidified $\mathrm{K}_{2}\mathrm{Cr}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7}$ and neutral $\mathrm{KMnO}_{4}$ have the ability to oxidise $\mathrm{I}^{-}$ to $\mathrm{I}_{2}$ independently.

Statement II : Manganate ion is paramagnetic in nature and involves $\mathrm{p}π-\mathrm{p}π$ bonding.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Statement I: $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}$ oxidises iodide ($2~\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}+2\mathrm{I}{}^{-}\longrightarrow 2\mathrm{Fe}{}^{2+}+\mathrm{I}{}_{2}$) and acidified $\mathrm{K}{}_{2}\mathrm{Cr}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{7}$ oxidises $\mathrm{I}{}^{-}$ to $\mathrm{I}{}_{2}$, but neutral or faintly alkaline $\mathrm{KMnO}{}_{4}$ oxidises iodide to iodate, $2~\mathrm{MnO}{}_{4}{}^{-}+\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}+\mathrm{I}{}^{-}\longrightarrow 2\mathrm{MnO}{}_{2}+2\mathrm{OH}{}^{-}+\mathrm{IO}{}_{3}{}^{-}$, so Statement I is false.

Statement II: manganate, $\mathrm{MnO}{}_{4}{}^{2-}$, contains Mn(VI) with one unpaired $3d$ electron and is paramagnetic, but its tetrahedral Mn–O $π$ bonds are $dπ$–$pπ$ bonds, not $pπ$–$pπ$, so Statement II is false.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift

text:
In Carius method of estimation of halogen, $0.45\mathrm{g}$ of an organic compound gave $0.36\mathrm{g}$ of $\mathrm{AgBr}$. Find out the percentage of bromine in the compound.

(Molar masses : $\mathrm{AgBr}=188\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1};\mathrm{Br}=80\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Mass of organic compound $=0.45\mathrm{gm}$

Mass of $\mathrm{AgBr}$ obtained $=0.36\mathrm{gm}$

$\therefore$ Moles of $\mathrm{AgBr}=\frac{0.36}{188}$

$\therefore$ Mass of Bromine $=\frac{0.36}{188}\times 80=0.1532\mathrm{gm}$

$\therefore %\mathrm{Br}$ in compound $=\frac{0.1532}{0.45}\times 100=34.04%$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift

options: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

text:
$2\mathrm{NO}+2\mathrm{H}_{2}\to \mathrm{N}_{2}+2\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

The above reaction has been studied at $800^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$. The related data are given in the table below

  
    Reaction serial number
    Initial Pressure of $H_{2}/kPa$
    Initial Pressure of $NO/kPa$
    Initial rate $\left (\frac{-dp}{dt}\right )/(kPa/s)$
  

  
    1
    65.6
    40.0
    0.135
  
  
    2
    65.6
    20.1
    0.033
  
  
    3
    38.6
    65.6
    0.214
  
  
    4
    19.2
    65.6
    0.106
  

The order of the reaction with respect to NO is $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the rate of reaction ( $r$ ) is as

$\mathrm{r}=\mathrm{K}[\mathrm{NO}]^{n}[\mathrm{H}_{2}]^{\mathrm{m}}$

From $1^{\text{st}}$ data

$0.135=\mathrm{K}[40]^{\mathrm{n}}\cdot (65.6)^{\mathrm{m}}...(1)$

From $2^{\text{nd}}$ data

$0.033=\mathrm{K}(20.1)^{\mathrm{n}}\cdot (65.6)^{\mathrm{m}}...(2)$

On dividing equation (1) by equation (2)

$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{0.135}{0.033}=\left (\dfrac{40}{20.1}\right )^{n} \\  \\ 4=(2)^{n} \\  \\ \therefore n=2 \\  \\ \therefore \text{Order of reaction w.r.t. NO is}2. \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift

text: The molar heat capacity for an ideal gas at constant pressure is $20.785\mathrm{J}\mathrm{K}^{-1}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$. The change in internal energy is $5000\mathrm{J}$ upon heating it from $300\mathrm{K}$ to $500\mathrm{K}$. The number of moles of the gas at constant volume is $____________$. [Nearest integer] (Given:  $\mathrm{R}=8.314\mathrm{J}\mathrm{K}^{-1}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{p}}=20.785\mathrm{J}\mathrm{K}^{-1}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{and}\Delta \mathrm{U}=\mathrm{nC}_{\mathrm{v}}\Delta \mathrm{T} \\  \\ \therefore \quad \mathrm{nC}_{\mathrm{v}}=\dfrac{5000}{200}=25 \end{array}$

and we know that

$\begin{array}{l} C_{p}-C_{v}=R \\  \\ 20.785-\dfrac{25}{n}=8.314 \\  \\ n=\dfrac{25}{(20.785-8.314)}=2 \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift

text: At $310\mathrm{K}$, the solubility of $\mathrm{CaF}_{2}$ in water is $2.34\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{g}/100\mathrm{mL}$. The solubility product of $\mathrm{CaF}_{2}$ is $____________$ $\times 10^{-8}(\mathrm{mol}/\mathrm{L})^{3}$. (Given molar mass : $\mathrm{CaF}_{2}=78\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{CaF}_{2}⇌^{\mathrm{s}}\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}_{\mathrm{s}}+2\mathrm{F}^{-}_{2\mathrm{s}}$

$\begin{array}{ll} \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{sp}} & =\mathrm{s}(2\mathrm{s})^{2} \\  \\ =4\mathrm{s}^{3} \end{array}$

Solubility $(\mathrm{s})=2.34\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{g}/100\mathrm{mL}$

 $=\frac{2.34\times 10^{-3}\times 10}{78}$ mole $/$ lit

 $=3\times 10^{-4}\mathrm{mole}/\mathrm{lit}$

$\therefore \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{sp}}=4\times \left (3\times 10^{-4}\right )^{3}$

$\begin{array}{l} =108\times 10^{-12} \\  \\ =0.0108\times 10^{-8}(\mathrm{mole}/\mathrm{lit})^{3} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \therefore \text{value in the blank}=0.0108\approx 0 \end{array}$

In JEE Main 2022, Section B answers are rounded off to the nearest integer, and the official NTA answer is 0.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift
